title: Google Maps is failing to complete basic searches for some users
summary: Google Maps on the web reportedly can’t find ‘restaurants’ or other broad searches.
body: Credit: Akshay Gangwar / Android Authority TL;DR Users are reporting that general searches aren’t working in Google Maps. When searching for something nonspecific, like restaurants, users are reportedly getting an error that suggests the search was misspelled. It appears that the issue is limited to the browser version. If you need help trying to find shops, restaurants, museums, or other locations around you, the search function in Google Maps can often come in handy. Just type in what you’re looking for and a list of suggestions will be there for you to peruse. Normally, that’s the case, but it seems a new bug may have broken this feature for some. There is a growing number of reports highlighting an issue with Google Maps searches. It appears that when looking for something specific, like the name of a building, the search feature will do its job. However, when you look for something nonspecific, like restaurants, you’ll get an error message.

title: Verizon is finally catching up with Motorola’s latest foldables
summary: The Moto Watch Ultra also makes its way to the carrier’s shelves.
body: TL;DR Verizon has announced nationwide availability of the Razr Fold, Razr Plus (2026), the Swarovski edition Razr (2026), along with the Moto Watch Ultra. Surprisingly, the Razr Fold and the Swarovski-branded Razr (2026) have a steeper price tag than their unlocked counterparts. Verizon is offering the Moto Watch Ultra for free after monthly credits if you bring a device or buy a new one from the carrier. Motorola’s first book-style foldable, the Razr Fold (2026) , reached US shelves in May this year, alongside the 2026 iterations of the Razr Ultra, Razr Plus, and the entry-level Razr. Earlier this month at IFA 2026, Motorola also took the wraps off the Swarovski edition Razr (2026) and the Moto Watch Ultra. It’s taken a while, but all models (except one) are now officially available via Verizon. The carrier has announced the nationwide availability of the Razr Fold (2026), alongside the Razr Plus (2026), and the Swarovski-branded Razr (2026). Verizon will also offer the Moto Watch Ultra for free through bill credits if you buy a Motorola device or bring your existing phone, though customers will need to add a new watch line.

title: "سامحونا".. مدرب اليمن يجلد لاعبيه بعد الفضيحة أمام الإمارات
summary: إهمال جماعي
body: إهمال جماعي بلهجة غاضبة ونبرة اعتذار لم يعهدها الجمهور اليمني، خرج الجزائري نور الدين ولد علي عن صمته ليفتح النار على لاعبيه، فبعد أقل من 90 دقيقة من مباراة أولى كارثية، لم يبحث المدرب عن أعذار واهية، بل وجه اتهاماً مباشراً وقاسياً وصف فيه ما حدث بـ "الإهمال الجماعي"، في ليلة سوداء انتهت برباعية إماراتية مذلة في افتتاح مشوار اليمن بخليجي 27. شن الجزائري نور الدين ولد علي، مدرب المنتخب اليمني الأول لكرة القدم، هجوماً لاذعاً على لاعبيه، محملاً إياهم مسؤولية الخسارة الثقيلة أمام المنتخب الإماراتي برباعية نظيفة، الخميس، ضمن الجولة الأولى من منافسات المجموعة الثانية لبطولة كأس الخليج العربي "خليجي 27" المقامة في جدة. وفي مؤتمر صحفي عاصف عقب نهاية المباراة، قدم المدرب الجزائري اعتذاراً صريحاً للجماهير اليمنية التي احتشدت لدعم المنتخب، قائلاً: "للأسف، نقول للجماهير الحاضرة: سامحونا، فالإهمال كان عنوان مباراة اليوم". وأضاف: "تحدثت مع اللاعبين عن هذا الأمر، خصوصاً في الجانب الدفاعي، أمام فريق يملك لاعبين يتمتعون بجودة ومهارات فردية عالية. وبإذن الله، يكون المستقبل أفضل". شووف| المدرب الجزائري نور الدين ولد علي: نقول للشعب اليمني "سامحنا" لأننا لم نمنحك الفرحة ولم نسعدك #الإمارات_اليمن #خليجي_الديار_العربية27 #كأس_الخليج || #خليجي27 #قنوات_الكاس || #منصة_شووف pic.twitter.com/3tdczBPvYX — قن…

title: Pixel users report Bluetooth volume control issues with Android 17 QPR1
summary: Absolute volume is busted for some.
body: TL;DR Multiple users report that absolute volume is no longer working the way it used to on their Pixel devices as of Android 17 QPR1. We don’t know what’s causing this issue or whether a fix is in the works. As is often the case around significant OS updates, Pixel users have been reporting all kinds of issues since Android 17 QPR1 started rolling out. We’ve seen users complain about problems with performance, touch detection, reception, and then some. Today, we’ve seen some reports that Pixel owners are having trouble with volume control. Reddit user KaneNova posted on the Google Pixel subreddit today saying that since downloading the September update on their Pixel 10, absolute volume, which syncs volume levels on Bluetooth headphones and the device they’re streaming audio from, has stopped working.

title: Your Pixel Watch now flags your risk of hypertension and diabetes
summary: Pixel Watch's new Health Guardian feature brings BP, insulin resistance, and sleep quality trends.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel Watch 3 and newer models are receiving the promised Health Guardian features. These include blood pressure and insulin resistance trends, as well as sleep quality analysis. The features are now available for free on the Pixel Watch, while Fitbit Air users will have to pay for them. At the launch of the Pixel Watch 5 , Google announced Health Guardian , a suite of features that detect trends from your health data and predict concerning physiologic changes, such as hypertension, diabetes, or sleep apnea. Google promised to roll it out “in fall,” and it’s now delivering on that commitment. Starting today, three vital Health Guardian features, including blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality, are now available for the Pixel Watch 3 and Watch 4, alongside the newly launched Pixel Watch 5. These three metrics join Breathing Emergency detection , which has been available on the Pixel Watch 4 and 5 since launch, but only in limited European countries.

While the struggles back in the day involved ensuring you had all the information, students today face the opposite problem , and Google wants to help fix that. Google is introducing three new Chrome features aimed at making that process a tad bit easier.

title: Google Home error warns users of movement even when they’re at home
summary: Users are getting flooded with notifications.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google Home users have been getting inundated by motion sensor alerts. Reportedly, notifications are being sent even when users are at home. It appears the issue may have resolved itself. If you want to improve the security of your home, it makes sense to install motion sensors and enable alerts. That way, you’ll be notified if there is ever suspicious activity happening at your home while you’re away. At the same time, you don’t exactly need to be warned about detected movement while you’re at your abode. For some users, it appears that Google Home thinks differently. Google Home users are reporting that they are getting inundated with motion alert notifications. No, this isn’t a large-scale burglary operation that’s currently underway. Rather, Google Home is warning of detected movement while users are at their residences. Which means anytime they make a move, Google Home is sending them an alert.

body: NASA/Ryan Kline In this Aug. 27, 2026, image, an Alta-X drone flies an advanced guidance and navigation system known as the Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution (SPLICE) experiment near NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California. Researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston developed SPLICE, which successfully completed simulated lunar descent and landing maneuvers during recent testing. Its technologies provide safe and precise landing for the Moon, Mars, icy worlds, and other destinations using specialized navigation, guidance, and processing techniques. title: Privacy Display on the Galaxy S27 Ultra could pick up this handy new trick
summary: Split-screen display dimming could make it to the early 2027 Samsung flagship.
body: TL;DR Prominent leaker Ice Universe claims the Galaxy S27 Ultra will introduce a split-screen Privacy Display feature, as seen on the Xiaomi 18 Pro series. This feature can cleverly dim just one app window in split-screen view, even when it’s resized. While Xiaomi appears to have more features tied to this privacy feature, the leaker notes that Samsung still has the upper hand in overall dimming capacity. Samsung set the industry standard by introducing Privacy Display on the Galaxy S26 Ultra , which enables hardware-level screen dimming to shake off shoulder surfers. While some brands have already revealed their own take on this feature, the freshly announced Xiaomi 18 Pro series takes it to another level with Smart Privacy Display. We’re now learning that Samsung may introduce at least one of the Xiaomi flagship’s privacy-oriented features in its early 2027 smartphone. Writing on X, leaker Ice Universe claims the Xiaomi 18 Pro’s unique split-screen privacy protection system will make its way to the Galaxy S27 Ultra . This split-screen privacy mechanism cleverly dims only one app, even as you resize it, while keeping the other in its normal, visible state.

title: Gmail is turning its stars and importance markers blue, and users aren’t happy
summary: Google says the change helps with accessibility, but users complain it flattens hierarchy and clutters the inbox.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google replaced Gmail’s default yellow stars and yellow importance chevrons with high-contrast, saturated blue markers to improve accessibility. However, users complain that the identical blue tones flatten the visual hierarchy, make email scanning harder, and add visual clutter. While there’s no way to revert the changes, you can manually select a yellow star preset (and re-star items) or hide importance chevrons entirely in Settings. Google is rolling out a visual overhaul to Gmail on the web, replacing its longstanding yellow stars and importance markers with a bright, high-contrast blue. While Gmail has gained plenty of genuinely practical upgrades recently, such as letting you copy 2FA codes directly without opening emails or leveraging AI overview search capabilities , this particular color switch has annoyed desktop users who rely on quick visual cues to scan their messages. In a post on X , the official Gmail team confirmed the change, explaining that it updated the default star and “Important” label colors from yellow to blue to meet modern accessibility standards and ensure inboxes are easier to read and more inclusive.

body: TL;DR Dolphin Emulator finally supports NetPlay on Android. The update lets users play online multiplayer with GameCube and Wii titles. Dolphin’s latest update also extends NetPlay to cross-platform instances. Dolphin Emulator is unquestionably one of the most popular retro game emulators for Android, Windows, Mac, and even a Steam Deck. It’s the first option enthusiasts turn to for Nintendo Wii and GameCube because of its upscaling, custom graphics mods, and easy Bluetooth and USB controller support, among other features. Another advantage of Dolphin is that it lets you play games originally designed for local multiplayer online, enabled by a feature called NetPlay. Traditionally, this feature required a specific mechanism to sync gameplay across multiple devices and was therefore limited to scenarios where all players are on the same operating system—and to desktop environments. That changes now with Dolphin announcing NetPlay support for Android and opening it up for cross-platform gameplay. body: TL;DR Qualcomm shares that Snapdragon X-series laptops are getting Linux support. Debian compatibility should roll out sometime later in 2026. Ubuntu is planning support for Snapdragon X2 devices early next year. It’s taken a couple decades, but something big has finally started happening for how we get computing done on laptops. After years of trying to be tiny desktop computers, running the same kind of chips that were never really designed for power efficiency, laptops began broadly embracing RISC computing — including models built around Qualcomm Snapdragon chips like the X series . This week at Qualcomm’s annual Snapdragon Summit, the company is sharing news of a big new upgrade for such models that power users are really going to love. For all the speed and battery life they offer, Snapdragon laptops have had at least one big blind spot: Linux. Even though different Snapdragon chips have been powering Android (with its deep Linux roots) devices for ages, initial Snapdragon X laptops lacked support for mainstream Linux distros .

If you rely a lot on Google Meet for your daily minimum dose of human contact, its “Take notes for me” feature is a godsend. As the name suggests, it automatically takes written notes for you, letting you stay more present in virtual meetings. Initially introduced for Workspace accounts, the feature was recently made available to regular Google users and has even expanded to real-life meetings and conversations . Now, Google is adding another layer to the feature that makes it even more useful. Google recently announced “Quick notes” as an extension to Take notes for me in Meet. title: I’ve used Razr phones for 20 years, and Motorola’s secret weapon hasn’t changed
summary: Motorola understands who buys its phones.
body: I’ve used Motorola phones longer than I’d like to admit. The Nokia 5160 I carried around in high school will always hold a special place in my heart, but Motorola soon became my preferred brand. I remember how jealous I was when my parents bought StarTACs. It’s hard to describe what a shift that device was for cell phones. Moto proved that the phones in our pockets could be smaller and more stylish, and the company wasn’t done there. The original Razr was a revelation when it was released in 2004. You didn’t want to buy anything else at the time, and it was hard to go anywhere without seeing someone use one. It’s why Motorola’s recent success isn’t a surprise. The company has maintained a consistent theme over the last two decades, and it doesn’t take much to see where that all began and how it translates perfectly to this current crop of Razrs.

title: The Sleenova SoundMask fixed my biggest issue with sleep earbuds
summary: Speakers next to your ears instead of inside them is a big deal for a side sleeper like me.
body: I’ve tested a handful of sleep earbuds over the years, and no matter how small they get, I haven’t found a pair that doesn’t create pressure in my ears while sleeping on my side, which can be uncomfortable. The Sleenova SoundMask avoids that problem with speakers built into the sides of a sleep mask that sits next to your ears. After a few nights with it, it became a pretty reliable tool for getting a good night’s rest, with its own tradeoffs to sleep earbuds. No more sore ears The SoundMask is very comfortable. Rather than pressing flat against your eyelids, there’s a contoured cavity that lifts the fabric off your eyes entirely, so you can blink and move your eyes freely without anything rubbing against them. There is ample padding around the eyes and nose, so that I could sleep face-down into a pillow without discomfort. It also blocks out light surprisingly well. I couldn’t see anything while wearing it, even in a fully lit room.

title: Garmin is bringing crucial life-saving and health features to several smartwatches

The company offers several smartwatches and screenless fitness trackers , and it regularly improves them with software updates. Now, it is adding useful new features to several of its smartwatches, including the Fenix 8 series, the Venu 4 and X1, the Forerunner 70 and 170, and more. The Venu 4 now supports fall detection, which will automatically send a message with the user’s live location to selected contacts for assistance. You can keep the feature active all day or enable it for specific activities. It’s worth noting that Garmin watches have supported fall detection, but it could only be enabled during specific outdoor activities. This update finally lets Venu 4 users enable fall detection all the time if needed.

title: Google Sheets now plays more nicely with your imported Excel spreadsheets
summary: Sheets also brings improvements for handling pivot tables.
body: TL;DR Google Sheets now lets users drag and drop rows or columns in pivot tables. It also maintains data hierarchy when moving rows or columns with nested child items. It now also preserves custom-sorted pivot tables when importing Excel spreadsheets. The last few months have been really great for Google Sheets users. Google has steadily rolled out new updates and features, introduced useful add-ons , and improved support for pivot tables . Now, it’s making it easier for users to manipulate pivot tables directly in Sheets. Google announced today that Sheets can now preserve custom sorting in pivot tables imported from Excel spreadsheets. Previously, Sheets reverted pivot tables to a standard alphanumeric sort order. However, it will now maintain any custom sort you’ve applied within Excel so you can easily move between the two apps. Exporting a Sheets file to an Excel spreadsheet also maintains the exact sorting order of your pivot tables.

Good Lock is supposed to give Galaxy owners more control over how One UI looks, but one Galaxy S26 Ultra user has found their carefully arranged lock screen doing its own thing after updating to One UI 9.
